subs.label: Horror
subs.axis: Axis: by the source of fear: the dead and the damned, national schools of the supernatural, classic and natural monsters, science and the body, the mind, human killers, gore, then the forms (found footage, anthology) and comedy last.

leaves.label: Ghost Film
leaves.defn: A horror film whose threat is the spirit of a dead person acting on the living, outside a single haunted dwelling (The Phantom Carriage, The Sixth Sense, Mama, The Devil's Backbone). A ghost bound to one house goes to the Haunted House Film; a Japanese onryō to J-Horror.
leaves.see: A4-2 Haunted House Film; A4-9 J-Horror; A4-3 Curse Film
leaves.axis: by how the dead reach the living: literary apparition, vengeful spirit, the medium who sees them, the place they are bound to

leaves.label: Haunted House Film
leaves.defn: A horror film whose threat is a dwelling or building itself, haunted by presences that menace whoever lives in or visits it (The Haunting, Poltergeist, The Conjuring, The Shining). A house haunted by a single cursed Japanese spirit goes to A4-9 J-Horror.
leaves.see: A4-1 Ghost Film; A4-4 Possession & Exorcism Film
leaves.axis: by who confronts the house: literary classic, besieged family, professional investigators, the institution, the grieving modern household

leaves.label: Curse Film
leaves.defn: A horror film whose engine is a curse or rule-bound supernatural pursuit that is laid, summoned or passed on, so that knowing the rules is survival (It Follows, Candyman, Ouija, Final Destination). The Japanese curse cycle (Ringu) goes to A4-9 J-Horror.
leaves.see: A4-9 J-Horror; A4-1 Ghost Film; A4-20 Killer Toy Film
leaves.axis: by how the curse is caught: laid and passed on, summoned by saying or believing a legend, carried by an object or game, death's own design

leaves.label: Possession & Exorcism Film
leaves.defn: A horror film whose threat is a demon or spirit inhabiting a human body, usually met by an exorcism (The Exorcist III, The Rite, The Possession, Under the Shadow). A demon that besieges a house rather than a body goes to A4-2 or A4-5.
leaves.see: A4-5 Satanic Film; A4-6 Religious Horror
leaves.axis: by the rite and tradition: the Exorcist cycle, Catholic exorcist procedurals, the possessed child or woman at home, jinn, dybbuk and other non-Christian possession

leaves.label: Satanic Film
leaves.defn: A horror film whose source of fear is Satan, his worshippers or the demonic hosts of Hell (The Omen, The Devil Rides Out, Hereditary, Hellraiser, The Evil Dead). A single possessed body goes to A4-4; nuns and convents to A4-6.
leaves.see: A4-4 Possession & Exorcism Film; A4-7 Witchcraft Horror
leaves.axis: by the form evil takes: the Antichrist child, the cult, the Devil in person, a demonic outbreak, Hell's otherworld, angels at war

leaves.label: Religious Horror
leaves.defn: A horror film whose fear grows from faith itself: convents, saints, zealotry and sacred ritual (The Nun, Saint Maud, Immaculate, Alucarda). Exorcism plots go to A4-4; Satanist cults to A4-5.
leaves.see: A4-4 Possession & Exorcism Film; A4-5 Satanic Film

leaves.label: Witchcraft Horror
leaves.defn: A horror film whose threat is a witch, a coven or a practitioner of black magic (Suspiria, The Craft, The Lords of Salem, The Boxer's Omen). Rural pagan communities go to A4-8 Folk Horror.
leaves.see: A4-8 Folk Horror; A4-5 Satanic Film; A4-13 Indonesian Horror
leaves.axis: by the craft: the witch and coven, then sorcery and black magic rituals

leaves.label: Folk Horror
leaves.defn: A horror film whose dread comes from a rural landscape, its old beliefs and the community that keeps them (The Wicker Man, Witchfinder General, Midsommar, The Witch). A witch in a modern city goes to A4-7.
leaves.see: A4-7 Witchcraft Horror; A4-29 Backwoods Horror
leaves.axis: by where the old ways survive: British and Irish countryside, the pagan community, the wilderness, folk traditions elsewhere

leaves.label: J-Horror
leaves.defn: The Japanese horror wave from the late 1990s, built on vengeful onryō, technology as a channel for the dead and urban isolation, plus its Hollywood remakes (Ringu, Ju-on: The Grudge, Pulse, The Ring). Pre-modern Japanese ghost tales go to A4-10 Kaidan Film.
leaves.see: A4-10 Kaidan Film; A4-3 Curse Film; C9 Horror Anime
leaves.axis: by strand: the onryō curse cycle, techno-urban dread, then the Hollywood remakes of Asian horror

leaves.label: Kaidan Film
leaves.defn: A Japanese film of a pre-modern ghost or supernatural tale in the kaidan tradition (Ugetsu, Kwaidan, Onibaba, Kuroneko).
leaves.see: A4-9 J-Horror; A8 Historical & Period Film

leaves.label: Korean Horror
leaves.defn: A South Korean supernatural horror film drawing on shamanism, han and family guilt (A Tale of Two Sisters, The Wailing, Exhuma, Gonjiam: Haunted Asylum). Korean zombie films go to A4-18.
leaves.see: A4-9 J-Horror; A4-4 Possession & Exorcism Film

leaves.label: Thai Horror
leaves.defn: A Thai supernatural horror film built on phi spirits, Buddhist karma and village belief (Nang Nak, Shutter, The Medium, Death Whisperer). Thai horror-comedy goes to A4-38.
leaves.see: A4-13 Indonesian Horror; A4-9 J-Horror

leaves.label: Indonesian Horror
leaves.defn: An Indonesian supernatural horror film drawn from local folklore, black magic (ilmu hitam) and Islamic belief, from the Suzzanna era to the 2010s revival (Satan's Slaves, Impetigore, Mystics in Bali, KKN di Desa Penari).
leaves.see: A4-7 Witchcraft Horror; A4-12 Thai Horror

leaves.label: Jiangshi Film
leaves.defn: A Hong Kong horror-comedy of hopping corpses and the Taoist priests who fight them (Mr. Vampire). Kept as the named cycle; European vampires go to A4-16.
leaves.see: A4-16 Vampire Film; A4-38 Comedy Horror

leaves.label: Gothic Horror
leaves.defn: A period horror film in the Gothic tradition of castles, ancestral curses and literary monsters, from Universal and Hammer to modern revivals (Frankenstein, Horror of Dracula, Black Sunday, Crimson Peak). Dracula and vampire films go to A4-16; werewolves to A4-17.
leaves.see: A4-16 Vampire Film; A4-17 Werewolf & Shapeshifter Film; A8 Historical & Period Film
leaves.axis: by studio cycle and period: early gothic, Universal monsters, Corman's Poe cycle, Hammer, Italian gothic, later revivals

leaves.label: Vampire Film
leaves.defn: A film whose monster is a blood-drinking undead, from Dracula adaptations to vampire comedies and action franchises (Nosferatu, Let the Right One In, The Lost Boys, Underworld). Hopping corpses go to A4-14 Jiangshi Film.
leaves.see: A4-15 Gothic Horror; A4-14 Jiangshi Film
leaves.axis: by register: Dracula adaptations first, then art-house, comic, teen/romantic, action, and siege/plague vampires

leaves.label: Werewolf & Shapeshifter Film
leaves.defn: A horror film whose monster is a human who turns into a wolf or another beast (An American Werewolf in London, The Howling, Ginger Snaps, Cat People). Universal's The Wolf Man stays in A4-15.
leaves.see: A4-15 Gothic Horror; A4-19 Creature Feature

leaves.label: Zombie Film
leaves.defn: A horror film whose threat is the reanimated or infected dead, from voodoo to rage virus (Night of the Living Dead, 28 Days Later, Shaun of the Dead, Train to Busan). Lab reanimation played for gore-comedy goes to A4-37 Splatstick.
leaves.see: A5-19 Post-Apocalyptic Film; A4-37 Splatstick
leaves.axis: by what raises the dead: voodoo, Romero's ghouls, the Italian cycle, comedy, viral infection, action franchises, revenant drama

leaves.label: Creature Feature
leaves.defn: A horror film whose threat is an invented monster that is neither a real animal nor an alien (Creature from the Black Lagoon, Tremors, Gremlins, The Descent). Real animals go to A4-21 Natural Horror; aliens to A4-22; giant city-smashers to A5-6 Kaiju.
leaves.see: A4-21 Natural Horror; A4-22 Science Fiction Horror; A5-6 Kaiju
leaves.axis: by where the creature lives: water, underground, folklore and the demonic, small mischief-makers, prehistory and cryptids

leaves.label: Killer Toy Film
leaves.defn: A horror film whose threat is a doll, puppet, toy or animatronic come alive (Child's Play, Puppet Master, Annabelle, Five Nights at Freddy's). An AI android doll goes to A4-22.
leaves.see: A4-3 Curse Film; A4-22 Science Fiction Horror

leaves.label: Natural Horror
leaves.defn: A horror film whose threat is real animals or nature turned predator, including enlarged or mutated real species (Jaws 2, The Birds, Cujo, Them!, Long Weekend). Invented monsters go to A4-19.
leaves.see: A4-19 Creature Feature; A5-6 Kaiju
leaves.axis: by the attacker: sharks and sea beasts, reptiles, swarms and giant bugs, mammals and birds, nature itself

leaves.label: Science Fiction Horror
leaves.defn: A horror film whose threat comes from a science-fictional premise: aliens, space, experiments, contagion or machines (Alien, The Thing, Invasion of the Body Snatchers, The Fly). Bodily transformation as the point goes to A4-23 Body Horror; cosmic unknowability to A4-24.
leaves.see: A5 Science Fiction; A4-23 Body Horror; A4-24 Lovecraftian Horror
leaves.axis: by the scientific source of the threat: alien predator, alien replacement, space and remote stations, the lab, contagion, machines

leaves.label: Body Horror
leaves.defn: A horror film whose fear is the transformation, invasion or mutilation of the human body itself (Videodrome, Tetsuo: The Iron Man, The Substance, Titane). A creature born in a lab goes to A4-22.
leaves.see: A4-22 Science Fiction Horror; A4-32 New French Extremity
leaves.axis: by what happens to the body: Cronenbergian mutation, metamorphosis, surgery and beauty, infection and parasites

leaves.label: Lovecraftian Horror
leaves.defn: A horror film of cosmic dread before entities or realities beyond human comprehension (In the Mouth of Madness, Color Out of Space, The Void, The Mist).
leaves.see: A4-22 Science Fiction Horror; A4-5 Satanic Film

leaves.label: Psychological Horror
leaves.defn: A horror film whose terror lies in the mind: breakdown, trauma, doubled identity or unreal worlds, with any monster kept ambiguous (Repulsion, Jacob's Ladder, Get Out, The Babadook). A killer stalking victims goes to A4-28 Slasher Film.
leaves.see: A3 Thriller & Mystery; A4-26 Psycho-Biddy; A4-28 Slasher Film
leaves.axis: by where the horror sits: the unravelling mind, grief and family, the double, purgatory and unreality, social allegory, obsession and art, confinement

leaves.label: Psycho-Biddy
leaves.defn: A horror-thriller cycle built on an ageing woman as a deranged menace (What Ever Happened to Baby Jane?, Hush...Hush, Sweet Charlotte, Strait-Jacket).
leaves.see: A4-25 Psychological Horror

leaves.label: Home Invasion Film
leaves.defn: A horror or thriller film whose engine is intruders breaking into a home and besieging those inside (Funny Games, The Strangers, You're Next, Don't Breathe).
leaves.see: A3 Thriller & Mystery; A5-18 Dystopian Film
leaves.axis: by who holds the house: siege thrillers, masked strangers, then reverse invasions where the home is the trap

leaves.label: Slasher Film
leaves.defn: A horror film in which a stalking killer murders a group of victims one by one, often till a final girl remains (Halloween, Friday the 13th, A Nightmare on Elm Street, Scream). Rural killer clans go to A4-29; holiday-themed killers to A4-30.
leaves.see: A4-29 Backwoods Horror; A4-30 Holiday Horror; A3 Thriller & Mystery
leaves.axis: by phase of the form: proto-slashers, the big franchises, the golden age, supernatural killers, post-Scream revival, comic and meta slashers, retro and new-wave slashers, public-domain parodies

leaves.label: Backwoods Horror
leaves.defn: A horror film in which travellers stray into the countryside and are hunted by rural killers or inbred clans (The Texas Chain Saw Massacre, The Hills Have Eyes, Wrong Turn, Wolf Creek). Pagan rural communities go to A4-8 Folk Horror.
leaves.see: A4-28 Slasher Film; A4-8 Folk Horror
leaves.axis: by the killers: the Leatherface cycle, cannibal and mutant clans, lone predators of tourists, swamp and forest stalkers

leaves.label: Holiday Horror
leaves.defn: A horror film whose killer or curse is built around a named holiday and its rituals (Silent Night, Deadly Night, My Bloody Valentine, Krampus, Trick 'r Treat). The Halloween franchise stays in A4-28.
leaves.see: A4-28 Slasher Film; A4-36 Anthology Horror
leaves.axis: by holiday: Christmas, then other holidays and Halloween night

leaves.label: Splatter Film
leaves.defn: A horror film whose primary attraction is graphic gore and the spectacle of the opened body (Blood Feast, Guinea Pig 2: Flower of Flesh and Blood, Nekromantik, Ichi the Killer). Prolonged captivity and torture go to A4-33.
leaves.see: A4-33 Torture Porn; A4-37 Splatstick

leaves.label: New French Extremity
leaves.defn: The French-language extreme horror cycle of the 2000s, transgressive in violence and sexuality (High Tension, Inside, Martyrs, Frontier(s)).
leaves.see: A4-31 Splatter Film; A1 Movements & Schools

leaves.label: Torture Porn
leaves.defn: A horror film whose engine is captivity and the prolonged torture of victims (Saw, Hostel, The Collector, Would You Rather).
leaves.see: A4-31 Splatter Film; A4-25 Psychological Horror

leaves.label: Cannibal Film
leaves.defn: A horror film whose threat is people who eat people, including the Italian jungle cycle (Cannibal Holocaust, Cannibal Ferox, Raw, Ravenous). Rural killer families go to A4-29.
leaves.see: A4-29 Backwoods Horror; A4-31 Splatter Film

leaves.label: Found-Footage Horror
leaves.defn: A horror film presented as recovered recordings made by the characters (The Blair Witch Project, REC, Paranormal Activity, Lake Mungo). Sources are the form; the threat may be any.
leaves.see: A4-1 Ghost Film; A20 Experimental & Avant-Garde
leaves.axis: by the camera that records it: lost tapes, investigation crews, home video, faux broadcasts and mock documentaries, screens and livestreams, anthologies

leaves.label: Anthology Horror
leaves.defn: A horror film made of separate stories, usually joined by a frame (Dead of Night, The House That Dripped Blood, Creepshow 2, Southbound). Found-footage anthologies stay in A4-35.
leaves.see: A4-35 Found-Footage Horror; A4-30 Holiday Horror

leaves.label: Splatstick
leaves.defn: A horror comedy whose humour is excessive gore staged as slapstick (Evil Dead II, Bad Taste, Re-Animator, Deathgasm). Zombie splatstick such as Braindead stays in A4-18.
leaves.see: A4-38 Comedy Horror; A4-31 Splatter Film; A4-18 Zombie Film

leaves.label: Comedy Horror
leaves.defn: A film in which horror's monsters, killers or hauntings drive a comic engine (Ghostbusters, Beetlejuice, Stree, The Cabin in the Woods, Ready or Not). Gore-as-slapstick goes to A4-37; pure parody of horror films to A12.
leaves.see: A12 Comedy; A4-37 Splatstick
leaves.axis: by the comic engine: monster-rally spoof, supernatural comedy, Asian horror-comedy, creature comedy, camp and cult, dark satire, meta-horror

subs.label: Science Fiction
subs.axis: Axis: by the speculative premise: space, aliens, giant monsters, time and other realities, machines and biology, societies of the future and their ending, then soft and comic science fiction last.

leaves.label: Hard Science Fiction
leaves.defn: A science fiction film whose drama rests on plausible physics, biology and engineering, usually in spaceflight (2001: A Space Odyssey, The Martian, Interstellar, The Andromeda Strain). Space adventure with empires and aliens goes to A5-2.
leaves.see: A5-2 Space Opera; A5-5 First Contact
leaves.axis: by distance from Earth: orbit, Moon and laboratory; Mars; deep-space voyages

leaves.label: Space Opera
leaves.defn: A science fiction adventure of interstellar empires, wars and heroes on a grand scale (Star Wars, Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan, Dune, Avatar). Plausible spaceflight goes to A5-1.
leaves.see: A5-1 Hard Science Fiction; A5-3 Military Science Fiction
leaves.axis: by mode: the Star Wars and Star Trek sagas, planetary romance, space westerns, family space adventure

leaves.label: Military Science Fiction
leaves.defn: A science fiction film centred on soldiers, armies and future warfare (Starship Troopers, Battle Los Angeles, Universal Soldier, Ender's Game).
leaves.see: A5-4 Alien Invasion; A9 War Film

leaves.label: Alien Invasion
leaves.defn: A science fiction film in which extraterrestrials attack or occupy Earth (The War of the Worlds, Independence Day, They Live, Attack the Block). Peaceful contact goes to A5-5; alien horror to A4-22.
leaves.see: A5-5 First Contact & Alien Visitor; A4-22 Science Fiction Horror; A5-3 Military Science Fiction

leaves.label: First Contact & Alien Visitor
leaves.defn: A science fiction film about humanity meeting extraterrestrials who are not simply invaders: messages, visitors, friends and abductors (Arrival, E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, Starman, Fire in the Sky).
leaves.see: A5-4 Alien Invasion; A17 Children's & Family Film
leaves.axis: by the encounter: first contact, the visitor among us, the alien friend, abduction and UFO encounters

leaves.label: Kaiju
leaves.defn: A film of giant monsters that rampage through cities or fight each other, from Toho's Godzilla to its imitators (Godzilla, Gamera, King Kong, The Host). Ordinary-sized monsters go to A4-19.
leaves.see: A5-7 Tokusatsu; A4-19 Creature Feature
leaves.axis: by studio cycle: Toho Showa, later Godzilla eras, Gamera, Hollywood giants, kaiju films elsewhere

leaves.label: Tokusatsu
leaves.defn: A live-action special-effects superhero film in the Japanese tradition of costumed transforming heroes, including adaptations (Shin Ultraman, Shin Kamen Rider, Mighty Morphin Power Rangers: The Movie).
leaves.see: A5-6 Kaiju; B10 Children's Series

leaves.label: Time Travel Film
leaves.defn: A science fiction film whose premise is movement through time or a broken flow of time (Back to the Future, 12 Monkeys, Primer, Edge of Tomorrow).
leaves.see: A5-12 Artificial Intelligence & Robots; A5-9 Parallel Universe Film
leaves.axis: by what time travel does: tourism in time, changing the past, the loop, comic culture clash, messages across time

leaves.label: Parallel Universe Film
leaves.defn: A science fiction film whose premise is alternate worlds or versions of reality existing side by side (Another Earth, Coherence, Mr. Nobody, The One).
leaves.see: A5-8 Time Travel Film; A5-10 Simulated Reality

leaves.label: Simulated Reality
leaves.defn: A science fiction film whose premise is a manufactured reality: virtual worlds, game spaces, dream and memory technology (Inception, Total Recall, eXistenZ, Ready Player One). The Matrix films stay in A5-11 Cyberpunk.
leaves.see: A5-11 Cyberpunk; A5-9 Parallel Universe Film

leaves.label: Cyberpunk
leaves.defn: A science fiction film of high-tech, low-life futures: corporations, cyborgs, hackers and networked cities (Blade Runner, The Matrix, RoboCop, Tetsuo II: Body Hammer).
leaves.see: A5-10 Simulated Reality; A5-12 Artificial Intelligence & Robots; C2 Mecha & Science Fiction Anime

leaves.label: Artificial Intelligence & Robots
leaves.defn: A science fiction film whose premise is thinking machines: rogue computers, androids, robot companions and giant robots (The Terminator, Ex Machina, Short Circuit, Transformers). A killer AI as horror goes to A4-22.
leaves.see: A5-11 Cyberpunk; A4-22 Science Fiction Horror
leaves.axis: by the machine's role: uprising and war, synthetic person, companion, giant robot, uploaded mind

leaves.label: Biopunk
leaves.defn: A science fiction film whose premise is biotechnology: cloning, genetic engineering and chemical enhancement of humans and animals (The Boys from Brazil, Okja, Limitless, Mickey 17). Lab monsters as horror go to A4-22.
leaves.see: A4-22 Science Fiction Horror; A5-18 Dystopian Film

leaves.label: Lost World
leaves.defn: An adventure in which prehistoric creatures survive or are revived in the modern world (The Lost World, Jurassic Park, 65).
leaves.see: A5-15 Scientific Romance; A5-6 Kaiju

leaves.label: Scientific Romance
leaves.defn: A Verne- and Wells-type science adventure of submarines, inventions and fabulous journeys, and its retro-futurist pastiches (20,000 Leagues Under the Sea, Things to Come, Invention for Destruction).
leaves.see: A5-14 Lost World; A6 Fantasy & Adventure

leaves.label: Size-Change Film
leaves.defn: A science fiction film whose premise is people shrunk or enlarged (The Incredible Shrinking Man, Fantastic Voyage, Honey, I Shrunk the Kids, Downsizing).
leaves.see: A5-22 Science Fiction Comedy; A17 Children's & Family Film

leaves.label: Psionics
leaves.defn: A science fiction or horror film whose premise is psychic powers such as telekinesis, telepathy or teleportation (Scanners, Carrie, Jumper, Midnight Special).
leaves.see: A4-25 Psychological Horror; A7 Action & Martial Arts

leaves.label: Dystopian Film
leaves.defn: A science fiction film set in a future society organised as oppression (1984, Brazil, The Hunger Games: Mockingjay, Snowpiercer). A world after collapse goes to A5-19.
leaves.see: A5-19 Post-Apocalyptic Film; A5-13 Biopunk
leaves.axis: by the mechanism of control: the state, the lethal game, the YA system, control of age and birth, the class enclosure, the lawless city, absurdist satire

leaves.label: Post-Apocalyptic Film
leaves.defn: A science fiction film set during or after the collapse of civilisation (Threads, Mad Max: Fury Road, The Road, Planet of the Apes). The catastrophe itself as spectacle goes to A5-20.
leaves.see: A5-20 Disaster Film; A5-18 Dystopian Film; A4-18 Zombie Film
leaves.axis: by what ended the world and what follows: nuclear war, the wasteland, the last survivors, the apes, slow collapse, then comic and cult wastelands

leaves.label: Disaster Film
leaves.defn: A film whose spectacle is a large-scale catastrophe and the struggle to survive it (The Towering Inferno, Twister, Armageddon, Contagion). Life after the collapse goes to A5-19.
leaves.see: A5-19 Post-Apocalyptic Film
leaves.axis: by the catastrophe: earthquake, volcano and flood; cosmic impact; transport and structures; pandemic; storms and climate
secs: Cosmic Impacts & End of the World

leaves.label: Soft Science Fiction
leaves.defn: A science fiction film whose speculative conceit serves human, social or philosophical questions rather than technology or spectacle (Solaris, The Man from Earth, The Fountain, Hard to Be a God).
leaves.see: A5-1 Hard Science Fiction; A16 Drama

leaves.label: Science Fiction Comedy
leaves.defn: A film whose comic engine is a science-fictional premise, often aliens among ordinary people (The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, Kin-dza-dza!, Earth Girls Are Easy, Iron Sky).
leaves.see: A12 Comedy; A5-5 First Contact & Alien Visitor
